turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, give me one second, this screen is taking its own time. Right, can you tell me again what brought you in today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I already told the nurse. I'm pregnant and I'm having spotting, and these cramps. I'm really tired, can we not start from zero.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): I know, the note is half filled. Spotting and cramps, yes. How many weeks do you think you are?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): They said maybe eight to ten weeks, but I am not sure of my dates at all.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): When was the last period? Say it once more, I was on the wrong tab.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): It was around Diwali, or after Diwali, I can't say which. I didn't mark it.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Around Diwali or after. So we cannot fix a proper date from that. Any bleeding before this spotting?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing in between. This spotting is new.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the spotting itself, how many days?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days... no, wait, it started Sunday night, so that is five days now.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Five days. What colour, and how much? Are you soaking a pad?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Brownish, sometimes pink. Not soaking. Maybe one panty liner in the whole day, and even that is not full.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cramps along with it?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, low down, like period pain, but not as bad. They come and go.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): One side or both, the middle?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Middle only. Not one side. Worse when I walk around the house, better if I lie down.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nausea, vomiting?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fainting, or pain at the shoulder tip?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No fainting, no shoulder pain. I am just very worried, that's all. I keep thinking I will lose this baby.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): I can see you're anxious. Let me just... the computer has hung again. Is your husband with you?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): He's waiting outside only. He is more tensed than me, but I told him to sit there.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fine. Any long-term problems? Thyroid, diabetes, blood pressure?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Thyroid. I am on thyroxine. No diabetes, no BP.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): What dose of thyroxine?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Twenty-five micrograms... sorry, no, fifty micrograms. Doctor increased it last month. I take it every morning, empty stomach.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fifty micrograms every morning. The nurse read out folic acid five milligrams once a day from your sheet. Is that what you're taking?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No, that is wrong. I take folic acid four hundred micrograms, one tablet at night. I don't know why she put five milligrams.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you and the nursing note don't match, and I can't see the strip from here. We'll leave the dose as unclear for now. Any other tablets?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I didn't start anything else.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to any medicine?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any operations in the past?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No operations. I had a normal delivery four years back, that's all. This is my second pregnancy.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or any alcohol?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never. I teach at a primary school, I took leave today because I couldn't manage the standing.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me check the blood pressure. It says 110 over 70... no, sorry, wrong row, it's 118 over 74. Pulse is 90.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): At the pharmacy machine last week it was lower, but okay, whatever.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): That was a different day, I'll go with today's reading. Abdomen is soft. There is mild tenderness low down in the centre, no guarding, no rigidity.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): It hurts a bit when you press, yes. Can you be quick, I'm uncomfortable.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't do an internal examination today. A scan will tell us more, and it's kinder.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): So will you do the scan? I've been waiting long enough already.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll book the ultrasound for tomorrow morning, and you can go home and rest today.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Tomorrow? The spotting was a bit more this morning, and I'm telling you I'm scared. Also, actually, I should say, I have been feeling sick.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sick how? You said no nausea just now.

[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I know, I said no. But in the mornings I feel nauseous, and I vomited day before yesterday, and a little yesterday also. Not today yet. I didn't want to make a big thing, I'm just exhausted.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, so there is morning nausea, and you vomited twice, not today. With the bleeding a bit heavier this morning, I'm changing the plan. Don't wait till tomorrow.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): So today itself?
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. Scan today, transvaginal ultrasound, in our scan room before you leave. And blood tests today: serum beta hCG, haemoglobin, blood group and Rh.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Transvaginal, meaning internal scan? I am already so uncomfortable.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, internal scan, it's the proper one at this stage. It won't harm the pregnancy. Empty your bladder before it, the staff will guide you.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. What do you think is happening? Just tell me straight, don't soften it.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression is a threatened miscarriage. I also cannot rule out an ectopic until we see the scan, even though the pain is in the middle and not one-sided.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Ectopic. God. My husband should hear this, can I call him in?
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, call him. He can sit, he doesn't have to talk if he doesn't want.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): He's come in. He'll just sit there. Please don't ask me to repeat the whole story again, I'm too tired.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't. For him, briefly: early pregnancy, spotting and cramps, we need the scan and the bloods today, we don't have a firm diagnosis yet.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): And the folic acid, which one do I continue? I'm confused now.

[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Continue folic acid daily, whichever tablet you actually have at home, until we sort the dose. Don't start any hormone tablets. I was going to give progesterone today, but I'll hold that until the scan shows what is inside.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. And if the bleeding gets worse tonight?
[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you soak through a pad in one hour, or the pain becomes severe, or you feel faint, go to emergency straight away. Don't wait for me.
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): And if it stays like this only?
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then come back to my clinic in two days, with the reports. We'll go through the scan together.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days. What about work, and, um, relations?
[SEG0069] person_1 (DOCTOR): No school till we have the scan result, and avoid intercourse till then. Rest at home, lie down when the cramps come. Keep drinking water.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm very anxious, I hardly slept last night. Is that going to affect the baby?

[SEG0071] person_1 (DOCTOR): Lack of sleep won't cause a miscarriage. Try to rest. The reports will guide us, not the worrying. Go to the lab first, then the scan room, and I'll see you in two days unless emergency happens before that.

spec.situation: Woman about 8-10 weeks pregnant with spotting and cramps; unsure of dates ('the last period was around Diwali, or after'); anxious; partner waits outside then joins. Scan and blood tests planned today, strict return advice.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Doctor says don't start hormone tablets and holds progesterone; 'other' hormone tablets not explicitly stated.
bad.text: Do not start progesterone or other hormone tablets until the scan shows what is inside (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)
